industry: Independent Power Producer / Nuclear & Fossil Generation
thesis: Talen Energy is an independent power producer with ~13 GW of generation capacity, anchored by the 2.5 GW Susquehanna nuclear plant — the largest single nuclear facility in the PJM interconnection. The company emerged from Chapter 11 in 2023 with a clean balance sheet and is now a prime beneficiary of the AI data center power demand surge, having signed a landmark co-location deal with Amazon/AWS at Susquehanna. Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $374M, and the company raised FY2026 guidance to $2.03–2.23B adjusted EBITDA and $1.20–1.35B adjusted FCF after completing the Cornerstone Acquisition (Waterford, Darby, Lawrenceburg gas plants). PJM capacity auction prices surging from $29/MW-day to $330/MW-day provide a powerful structural tailwind. The stock is down ~23% YTD from its highs, creating an attractive entry. Key risks are regulatory challenges to nuclear co-location, GAAP losses from Cornerstone integration, and generation concentration in PJM.

base_case.assumptions: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA near the midpoint of the $2.03–2.23B guidance range, with FY2027 growth from Cornerstone and capacity revenue escalation. Market applies an 8–10x EV/EBITDA multiple, reflecting IPP status with nuclear premium. Stock recovers modestly from recent pullback.

risks: FERC or PJM regulatory actions restrict nuclear co-location or behind-the-meter data center arrangements
PJM capacity auction pricing normalizes lower than the current $330/MW-day peak
Susquehanna nuclear outage or operational disruption materially impacts earnings
Natural gas price decline compresses margins at Cornerstone gas plants
Macro or power market downturn reduces demand and pricing for merchant generation
